title: Ephemeral metric gaps in rollout health checks and remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a staged canary rollout on 2026-02-26 we observed a staggered latency regression affecting only canary traffic. The incident surfaced as increased canary failures in the rollout UI but failed to trigger any alert or SLO breach because the health-check metrics for rollout decisions were emitted as ephemeral internal gauges that were not routed into our metrics aggregator (Prometheus -> Cortex). As a result, dashboards and SLOs showed healthy aggregated signals while the canary slice experienced degraded latency and queue pressure.

Root cause analysis:
- Health probes used a transient sampling path implemented inside the rollout agent; those probes emitted metrics via a local aggregator that was disabled in production for perf reasons.
- There was no contract test or metric-ownership entry to ensure the rollout probe was backed by a persisted time-series.
- Existing dashboards relied on long-running aggregate metrics (request_rate, p95) and did not include short-window, per-tenant canary breakdowns or queue-depth signals.
- Trace sampling for canary flows was set to 1% which missed this narrow regressions; traces that showed KV cache thrashing were not captured.

Impact: The UI allowed a canary to progress for ~18 minutes before engineers noticed via user-reported throttles. No customer-wide outage occurred, but a small subset of customers on canary experienced elevated error rates and tail latency.

Decision & trade-offs:
- We will persist the rollout health probe metrics into our central metrics pipeline to guarantee coverage for both short-window alerting and dashboarding. This increases cardinality slightly (tenant x rollout) and therefore we will aggregate on scrape side and add retention rules to the metrics store to bound cost.
- Increase trace sampling for canary-tagged requests from 1% to 10% for the first 30 minutes of each rollout; will revert to baseline after the canary completes. This trades a small tracing storage cost for better root-cause visibility during high-risk windows.
- Introduce a canary-specific dashboard and alerting rule that evaluates short-window (1m/5m) p95, error rate, and queue-depth with per-tenant slices to prevent silent regressions.

Work to be done (high-level):
1) Add a metric contract and instrumentation for rollout health probe to emit persisted counters/gauges routed to Prometheus (ENG-329411).
2) Create a canary telemetry aggregator rule with cardinality bucketing and retention (ENG-329412).
3) Build per-tenant canary dashboard panels + short-window alerts in Grafana; wire to PagerDuty + runbook.
4) Adjust tracing sampler and add automatic sampler bump for rollout windows.
5) Update rollout playbook and add a pre-release checklist that verifies metric persistence and dashboard coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout probe metrics are emitted to the central metrics pipeline and visible in Prometheus within 60s of emission.
Grafana dashboard contains per-tenant canary panels for p95, error_rate, and queue_depth with 1m and 5m windows.
Alert policy triggers when canary p95 increases by >2x baseline or error_rate >0.5% for 3 consecutive 1m buckets and pages on-call.
Trace sampling increase is implemented for canary-tagged requests and verified by end-to-end test showing sampled traces during a synthetic canary run.
Runbook updated and linked from the alert; runbook contains triage steps, rollback checklist, and ownership.
Estimate and retention rules documented; cardinality cost impact evaluated and approved by infra cost lead.
subtasks: ENG-329411: Persist rollout-agent probes to central metrics
ENG-329412: Canary aggregator and retention rules
ENG-329414: Trace sampling bump for rollout windows
ENG-329415: Runbook and pre-release checklist update
comments: 2026-02-27 - Aisha Patel: Initial incident write-up and root-cause hypotheses. Filed ENG-329411/329412 as follow-ups. Notifying infra and telemetry owners.

2026-03-01 - Miguel Romero: Implemented initial metrics emitter in staging; metrics appear in staging Prometheus but need labels trimmed to avoid high-cardinality. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-agent/pull/274

2026-03-02 - Priya Nair (Telemetry): Reviewed PR and requested adding 'rollout_id' and 'tenant_bucket' normalization to limit cardinality. Also requested an integration test. See Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Canary+Metric+Contract

2026-03-03 - SRE Lead (Evan Liu): Approved retention rule proposal (90d -> 7d for canary buckets) and recommended a roll-forward for the metrics exporter to avoid missing samples during node restarts.

2026-03-04 - Miguel Romero: Deployed sampling bump to canary sampler; verified increased trace rate in synthetic canary test. Traces show KV cache eviction spikes correlated with latency. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tracing-config/pull/58
